summary.tldr: Requires the Health Minister to develop a national framework to improve women’s health, with consultations, conferences and reports to Parliament.
what_it_does: Requires the Minister of Health to develop a national framework on women’s health, after consulting other ministers, provincial and territorial health officials, Indigenous peoples, and other stakeholders.
Says the framework must address health research, innovation, commercial use of research, private sector collaboration, training for health workers, primary care, prevention and better access to care.

Requires the framework to include ways to improve access for women in rural and remote communities, equity-deserving groups, 2SLGBTQI+ and Indigenous women, visible minority women, and women without steady care.
Requires the Minister to hold at least one conference to help develop the framework, then another conference at least every three years to get input on its progress and results.
Requires the Minister to try to keep women’s health on the agenda at federal, provincial and territorial health ministers’ meetings.
Requires a report on the framework’s priorities and plan within one year, and a follow-up report on its effectiveness within five years, with both reports tabled in Parliament and posted online.
who_it_affects: Women in rural and remote communities
summary.background: The bill says it would create a national framework to promote, enhance and protect women’s health as a matter of national concern.
